## 2. The acquired period space

For the already acquired prefix h_t=(Q_1,...,Q_t), define

    B_i(x,v)=Q_i(x+v)+Q_i(x)+Q_i(v)+Q_i(0),
    L_t=intersection_(i<=t) rad B_i,
    A_t(v)=h_t(v)+h_t(0) on L_t,
    N_t=ker(A_t:L_t->F_2^t).                              (1)

All these are computed from the acquired quadratic ANFs. The polar matrices
are explicit alternating binary matrices. Find their common kernel, evaluate
the prefix on its basis, then take the kernel of that linear response map.
The response map is linear on L_t because all polar terms vanish there.
Dense Gaussian elimination and ANF evaluations suffice; naively performing
them for all n stages costs O(n^5) bit operations, with O(n^3) stored acquired
coefficients and checkpoint bases. No polynomial-identity oracle is used.

**Period lemma.** N_t is exactly the space of native translations preserving
the whole prefix at EVERY input:

    v in N_t <=> h_t(x+v)=h_t(x) for every x.             (2)

Indeed the difference is B_i(x,v)+Q_i(v)+Q_i(0). If it is identically zero,
setting x=0 kills the constant term, and the remaining bilinear dependence
forces v into every polar radical. Conversely (1) kills both terms. Hence
N_(t+1) is contained in N_t. Set N_0=V.

Every coset x+N_t lies in the prefix fibre through x. Bijectivity of Q makes
every true t-prefix fibre have exactly 2^(n-t) points. Consequently

    dim N_t <= n-t.                                      (3)

Call t an AFFINE CHECKPOINT precisely when the COMPUTED dimension equals
n-t. Under the correct-prefix and permutation promises, the inclusion and
cardinality give the much stronger fact

    h_t^-1(h_t(x))=x+N_t for every native witness x.        (4)

No fibre enumeration or latent coordinate recovery is needed to certify
this implication within the model. It is not recognition of arbitrary
source orders. A wrong learned prefix can pass the dimension test. A
computed dimension greater than n-t can trigger UNKNOWN, but passing that
test cannot remove the acquisition confidence allowance.

There is always a checkpoint at 0. There is one at n because a translation
preserving an injective complete Q must be zero. Write ALL true checkpoints

    0=tau_0<tau_1<...<tau_k=n,
    g(Q)=max_j(tau_j-tau_(j-1)).                          (5)

This is an a posteriori complexity parameter, not input to the learner. No
invariance under arbitrary reordering

## 2. Acquiring an exact frame inside an already certified fibre

Suppose the current prefix h_s=(Q_1,...,Q_s) has a certified full fibre

    A=x+U=h_s^-1(h_s(x)),    dim U=n-s.                  (1)

The certificate is an inductively justified mathematical implication under
the correct acquired-prefix and permutation promises, not an independent
recognition certificate for arbitrary source orders. Initially s=0, U=V
and A=V for any native x.

For a later acquired prefix length j>s, restrict the NEW coordinate block
to this known native carrier. Its period space is

    P(A,j)={v in U: Q_i(z+v)=Q_i(z)
                   for every z in A, s<i<=j}.           (2)

This is paid finite linear algebra on acquired quadratic programs. More
explicitly, compute

    L={v in U: B_i(w,v)=0 for all w in U, s<i<=j},
    ell_x(v)=(Q_i(x+v)+Q_i(x))_(s<i<=j),  v in L,
    P(A,j)=ker ell_x.                                   (3)

Choose the actual acquired basis of U. Every restricted polar matrix has
entries B_i(u_a,u_b). On L the displayed response is a linear map, and
the quadratic expansion proves (2)--(3) exactly. No derivative, global
coordinate oracle, hidden-input chart, or fibre enumeration is used.

The period space is independent of the origin chosen in A. If x'=x+w_0
with w_0 in U, its response on L changes by B_i(w_0,v)=0. Thus both the
test and its successful subspace depend on the actual affine carrier A,
which is determined by the fixed earlier prefix, rather than on an
unobserved choice of its witness.

Each coset z+P(A,j) in A lies in a j-prefix fibre. Every such fibre has
exactly 2^(n-j) points because Q is a permutation, so

    dim P(A,j)<=n-j.                                    (4)

If equality holds, it follows that EVERY j-prefix fibre inside A is one
whole P(A,j) coset. In particular, the new certified carrier for x is

    h_j^-1(h_j(x))=x+P(A,j).                            (5)

Every extension of the fixed s-prefix occurs inside A. Equation (5) is
therefore valid for all its extension labels, not just the currently
requested witness. The argument uses the known balanced-prefix sizes;
having a large period space alone would not suffice without that promise.

## 1. Changed observation contract, stated literally

Keep an unknown quadratic permutation Q:F_2^n->F_2^n, native chosen addresses
and actual fair bits, but do NOT assume every comparison is correct.
There is a fixed unknown set B with native uniform mass at most epsilon.
Whenever both submitted endpoints lie outside B, the answer equals the
lexicographic comparison of Q. Every comparison touching B can be arbitrary,
inconsistent with a total order, and adaptive to the full past and the
currently submitted inputs.

B and Q are fixed before the learner's fresh tapes. Allowing B to be chosen
after seeing a fresh address would defeat the argument: a small evolving
set could contain every queried point. A numerical upper bound epsilon
is a source-contract premise, not acquired by these comparisons. No
per-fibre accuracy, pointwise query-noise bound, independent noise, latent
sampler, label access, or supplied conditional frame is given.

The object to recover is the underlying Q and its closed procedures, NOT
an exact representation of arbitrary answers at corrupt endpoints. If the
actual oracle is a total order with arbitrarily reranked points in B, its
literal rank bits need not be Q's bits even outside B. That distinction
must not be erased in an after-expiry interpretation.

The difficulty is that some selected prefix fibres can be ENTIRELY bad.
A proof requiring each conditional fibre to have small corruption would
assume a stronger observation contract than the one above.

Condition the ideal analysis on a correct acquired Q prefix h_t. Its exact
witness sampler is either the global-checkpoint or the stronger conditional
affine-frame sampler. For a fresh uniformly distributed request X, sample

uniform marginal. More precisely, write

    N=2^(n-t),
